en: The state or characteristic of being good.
The good, nutritional, healthy part or content of something.

Fierce, intense, vehement.

ex.ja: この犬は鋭い臭覚をもっている。

en: obligatory; required or commanded by authority.
Of, being or relating to a mandate.
A sign or line that require the path of the disc to be above, below or to one side of it.

ex.ja: 年齢による差別は法律違反であり、退職が強制されるのは、ほんの少数の職業においてである。

The design and construction of machines.

ex.ja: あの修理工たちは時給一万円ももらっている。

en: Just, only; no more than, pure and simple, neither more nor better than might be expected.
Boundary, limit; a boundary-marker; boundary-line.
To decide upon the position of a boundary; to position it on a map.

mere.ety:
From Middle English mere, mer, from Anglo-Norman meer, from Old French mier, from Latin merus (“pure, unmixed, undiluted”), from Proto-Indo-European *mer- (“to sparkle, gleam”).
Cognate with Old English āmerian, āmyrian (“to purify, examine, revise”). The Middle English word was perhaps influenced by or conflated with sound-alike Middle English mere (“glorious, noble, splendid, fine, pure”), from Old English mǣre (“famous, great, excellent, sublime, splendid, pure, sterling”), from Proto-West Germanic *mārī, from Proto-Germanic *mērijaz.

ex.en: The merest mention of his name made her angry.
ex.ja: 彼の名前をほんの口に出しただけでも彼女は腹を立てた。

ex.ja: 私がそれを見つけたのは全くの偶然であった。

ex.en: You are no longer a mere child.
ex.ja: 君はもはや子供なんかではない。

en: An event that appears inexplicable by the laws of nature and so is held to be supernatural in origin.
A fortunate outcome that prevails despite overwhelming odds against it.
To affect by a miracle; to work a miracle upon.

miracle.ety: From Middle English miracle, from Old French miracle, from Latin mīrāculum (“object of wonder”), from mīror (“to wonder at”), from mīrus (“wonderful”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)meyh₂- (“to smile, to be astonished”). Doublet of milagro and miraculum. Partially displaced native wonder, from Old English wundor (“miracle, wonder”).

ex.en: Our escape was nothing short of a miracle.
ex.ja: われわれの脱出は奇跡というほかなかった。

ex.en: Christ is believed to have worked many miracles.
ex.ja: キリストは多くの奇跡を行ったと信じられている。

ex.en: His recovery was nothing short of a miracle.
ex.ja: 彼の回復は全く奇跡も同然であった。

en: A mixture of water and soil or fine grained sediment.
A plaster-like mixture used to texture or smooth drywall.
To make muddy or dirty; to apply mud to (something).
To make turbid.

mud.ety: From Middle English mud, mudde, mode, probably a borrowing from Middle Dutch mod, modde or Middle Low German mudde, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *mud-, *mudra- (“mud”), perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *mū-, *mew- (“moist”). Cognate with Saterland Frisian Mudde (“mud”), Middle High German mot (“mud”), Swedish modd (“slush”). Compare also suffixed variants English mother (“vinegar-forming sediment in alcohol”), West Frisian modder (“mud”), Dutch modder (“mud”), German Low German Mudder (“mud”), German Moder (“moldiness, mildew, decay”), Danish mudder (“mud”). en: The act of observing, and the fact of being observed (see observance)
The act of noting and recording some event; or the record of such noting.

observation.ety:
From Middle English observacion, borrowed from Middle French observacion. Also a borrowing from French observation and a learned borrowing from Latin observātiō(n-).
Morphologically observe + -ation.

ex.en: A careful observation will show you the difference.
ex.ja: 注意深く観察すれば違いがわかるでしょう。

ex.en: Science is based on very careful observations.
ex.ja: 科学は非常に綿密な観察に基づいている。

ex.en: His observation is sharp, but he says very little.
ex.ja: 彼は観察が鋭いがとても無口だ。

note.ja: ob（〜に向かって）+ serv（見守る）+ ation。注意深く見守ること →「観察・意見」。

en: To be under an obligation to give something back to someone or to perform some action for someone.
To have debt; to be in debt.

Cognate with Sanskrit ईष्टे (īṣṭe, “to own, possess”).

ex.ja: そんなに夜更かしするべきでないよ。

ex.en: You ought not to say such a thing.
ex.ja: そんなことは言うべきではない。

ex.en: Do what you ought to, come what may.
ex.ja: どんなことが起ころうと、なすべきことはしなさい。

en: A thing or being, event or process, perceptible through senses; or a fact or occurrence thereof.
A knowable thing or event (e.g. by inference, especially in science).

The declaration of belief in the principles of a religion; hence, one's faith or religion.

en: The region which the eye overlooks at one time; a view; a scene; an outlook.
A picturesque or panoramic view; a landscape; hence, a sketch of a landscape.
To search, as for gold.
To determine which minerals or metals are present in a location.

prospect.ety: From Middle English prospecte, from Latin prōspectus (“view, sight, prospect; panorama”), from prōspiciō (“to look forward”) + -tus (suffix forming action nouns), from pro (“before, forward”) + speciō, spiciō (“to look, to see”). ex.en: Our prospects for victory are excellent at the moment.
ex.ja: 今のところ、私たちが勝つ見込みは十分にある。

ex.ja: 彼女は有望な仕事に就いている。

ex.en: The prospects for our victory are excellent.
ex.ja: 僕らが勝利する見込みは十分ある。

A system or component that allows other components (subscribers) to receive notifications of something, such as an event.

en: The act of pulling back or withdrawing, as from something dangerous, or unpleasant.
The act of reversing direction and receding from a forward position.
To withdraw from a position, go back.
To withdraw military forces.

ex.ja: 彼は前進も後退もすまいと決めた。

A novice.
Non-professional; amateur
To be a rookie; to go through one's inexperienced learning period in a job, team, or organization.
To haze one or more rookies as an initiation ritual.

rookie.ety: Thought to be an alteration of recruit + -ie, or from rook (“a cheat”) + -ie. Another possible origin is Dutch broekie (short for broekvent (“a boy still in short trousers”)), a common term for a shipmate. Also suggested is Irish rúca (“an inexperienced person”).

ex.en: The rookie breathed new life into the team.
ex.ja: その新人はチームに新たな生気を吹き込んだ。

Any combination formed by layering one type of material between two layers of some other material.
To place (an item) physically between two other, usually flat, items.
To put or set between two other events in time.
Of a meal or serving size that is smaller than a dinner.

sandwich.ety: Named after its supposed inventor, the Earl of Sandwich (see Sandwich).

ex.ja: 俺のサンドイッチを食べたのはお前なのか？

ex.en: Can you make do with sandwiches for lunch?
ex.ja: お昼はサンドイッチでいいですか。

en: The act of disuniting two or more things, or the condition of being separated.
The act or condition of two or more people being separated from one another.

separation.ety: Attested in the 15th Century C.E.; from Middle English separacioun, from Old French separacion, from Latin separatio, separationem. Morphologically separate + -ion.

ex.en: The father and son met after a long separation.
ex.ja: 親子は久しぶりにあった。

ex.en: Meeting is the beginning of separation.
ex.ja: 会うは別れの始め。

ex.en: The separation of gold from sand is problematic.
ex.ja: 砂から金をより分けるのは難問だ。

en: One of a pair of long flat runners designed for gliding over snow or water.
One of a pair of long flat runners under some flying machines, used for landing.
To move on skis.
To travel over (a slope, etc.) on skis; to travel on skis at (a place), (especially as a sport).

ski.ety: From Norwegian ski, from Old Norse skíð (“stick of wood, snowshoe”), from Proto-Germanic *skīdą (“stick”), from Proto-Indo-European *skey- (“to cut, split”) (see also shed). Cognate with Old English sċīd (“stick of wood”) (modern shide), Old High German skit (Modern German Scheit (“log”)).

ex.en: He could ski well when he was young.
ex.ja: 彼は若いころスキーがうまかった。

ex.en: Tom said that he'd never tried water skiing.
ex.ja: トムは水上スキーをしたことがないと言った。

ex.en: Tom can ski almost as well as Mary.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーとほぼ同じぐらい上手にスキーができます。

en: An English silver penny first introduced by the Normans.
A penny issued in other countries, such as Scotland.
Of or relating to the currency of the United Kingdom, or former types of English or British coinage.
Of silver: being of standard quality.

sterling.ety: From Middle English sterling, possibly from Old English *steorling, from steorra (“star”) and -ling, in reference to the stars that appeared on certain English pennies. Alternatively, the first element may be *stēre, meaning “strong” or “stout” (compare the etymology of solidus).

en: One who performs surgery; a doctor who performs operations on people or animals.
A surgeonfish.

surgeon.ety: From Middle English surgien, borrowed from Anglo-Norman surgien, sirogen (Old French surgien et al.), from Vulgar Latin *chīrurgiānus, from Latin chīrūrgia (“surgery”), from chīrurgus (“surgeon”), borrowed from Ancient Greek χειρουργός (kheirourgós), from χείρ (kheír, “hand”) + ἔργον (érgon, “work”). ex.en: Besides being a surgeon, he was a famous writer.
ex.ja: 彼は外科医である上に著名な作家であった。

Cognate with West Frisian tsjeafte (“theft”), dialectal Dutch diefte (“theft”), obsolete German Diebde (“theft”), Icelandic þýfð (“theft”).

ex.en: Get 'em before they get you!
ex.ja: やられる前にやれ。

ex.en: It's a shoot-'em-up western.

en: A device that controls the flow of a gas or fluid through a space, such as a pipe, manifold, or plenum.
Such a device that admits fuel and air into the cylinder of an internal combustion engine, or one that allows combustion gases to exit.
To control (flow) by means of a valve.

ex.ja: すべてがトムの予言通りに進んでいる。

ex.en: Isn't there any way to predict how he'll act?
ex.ja: 彼がどのように行動するか予想する手はないものか。

ex.en: Just as predicted, he was thirty years of age.
ex.ja: イメージどおり、三十路くらいの人だったよ。

note.ja: pre（前もって）+ dict（言う）。前もって言う →「予言する・予測する」。

en: The act of pursuing.
A hobby or recreational activity, done regularly.

pursuit.ety: From Middle English pursuyte, from Old French poursuite, from the verb porsuir (“to pursue”).

ex.en: We are all in daily pursuit of happiness.
ex.ja: 我々はみな日々幸福を求めている。

ex.en: After a short pursuit, the police caught him.
ex.ja: ちょっと追跡して警官は彼を捕まえた。

ex.en: Most people live in pursuit of happiness.
ex.ja: たいていの人々は幸福を求めて生きている。

Writing that reminds of open payments.

en: To start (something) again that has been stopped or paused from the point at which it was stopped or paused; continue, carry on.
To start again after an interruption or pause.
A summary or synopsis.
A summary or account of education and employment experiences and qualifications; a curriculum vitae (often for presentation to a potentia…

resume.ety: From Anglo-Norman resumer, Middle French resumer, from Latin resumere, from re- + sumere (“to take”).

ex.en: I don't worry so much about my resume.
ex.ja: ぼくは履歴書なんか気にしないよ。

ex.en: Thank you for helping me write my resume.
ex.ja: 履歴書を書くの手伝ってくれてありがとう。

ex.en: He resumed his work after a short break.
ex.ja: 彼は短い休息の後、仕事を再開した。

note.ja: re（再び）+ sum（取る）+ e。再び取り上げる →「再開する」。名詞 résumé は「要約・履歴書」。

en: The back of any animal; especially the upper or projecting part of the back of a quadruped.
Any extended protuberance; a projecting line or strip.
To form into a ridge.
To extend in ridges.

ridge.ety:
From Middle English rigge, rygge, (also rig, ryg, rug), from Old English hryċġ (“back, spine, ridge, elevated surface”), from Proto-West Germanic *hrugi, from Proto-Germanic *hrugjaz (“back”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)krewk-, *(s)ker- (“to turn, bend”).
Cognate with Scots rig (“back, spine, ridge”), North Frisian reg (“back”), West Frisian rêch (“back”), Dutch rug (“back, ridge”), German Rücken (“back, ridge”), Swedish rygg (“back, spine, ridge”), Icelandic hryggur (“spine”). Cognate to Albanian kërrus (“to bend one's back”) and kurriz (“back”).

ex.en: Is this the bus for Park Ridge?
ex.ja: このバスは、パークリッジ行きですか。

A specialist in a particular branch of knowledge.

ex.ja: 彼らは彼を大学者とみなした。

en: An ethnic group larger than a band or clan (and which may contain clans) but smaller than a nation (and which in turn may constitute a na…
A tribal nation or people.
To distribute into tribes or classes; to categorize.

ex.en: Members of that tribe settled along the river.
ex.ja: その部族の民はその川沿いに住み着いた。

ex.en: Members of the tribe settled down along the river.
ex.ja: その部族のひとびとはその川沿いに定住した。

ex.en: There are quite a lot of tribes in the world.
ex.ja: 世界には実に多くの種族がいます。

en: Not favored by fortune.
Marked or accompanied by or resulting in misfortune.
An unlucky person; one who has fallen into bad circumstances.

unfortunate.ety: From un- + fortunate, doublet of infortunate.

ex.en: I picked a most unfortunate time to visit him.
ex.ja: あいにくの時に訪ねてしまった。

ex.en: There was an unfortunate incident at home.
ex.ja: 家で不幸な出来事があった。

ex.en: It was unfortunate that he lost his passport.
ex.ja: 不運なことに彼はパスポートを無くしてしまった。

en: Able to vary or be varied.
Likely to vary.
Something that is variable.
Something whose value may be dictated or discovered.

variable.ety: Borrowed into Middle English in the 14th century from Old French variable, from Latin variare (“to change”), from varius (“different, various”). Equates to English vary + -able.

ex.en: A song says a girl's mind is variable.
ex.ja: ある歌によれば、女心は変わりやすいそうだ。

ex.en: His opinions are variable.
ex.ja: 彼の意見は変化しやすい。

en: Of or relating to the reign of Queen Victoria from 1837 to 1901, or that period.
In a situation of poverty and social injustice; Dickensian.
A person born in or living in the Victorian period, or exhibiting characteristics of that period.
An item of furniture from that period.

Victorian.ety: From Victoria + -an (suffix forming adjectives and agent nouns), from the name of Queen Victoria (1819–1901), monarch of the United Kingdom.

ex.en: The apartment was furnished in the Victorian style.
ex.ja: そのアパートはビクトリア朝風の家具を揃えてあった。

en: The 14th letter of Classical and Modern Greek. The 15th in Ancient and Old Greek.
Either of a pair of hyperons having spin 1/2, which decay into a lambda particle and a pion.
A playing card showing a single pip, typically the highest or lowest ranking card in a game.
A die face marked with a single dot, typically representing the number one.
To pass (a test, interviews etc.) perfectly.
To defeat (others) in a contest; to outdo (others) in a competition.

ace.ety: Inherited from Middle English as, from Old French as, from Latin as, assis (“unity, copper coin, the unit of coinage”), probably borrowed from Etruscan. Doublet of as.

ex.en: I was within an ace of winning.
ex.ja: 私はもう少しで優勝するところだった。

ex.en: He was within an ace of success.
ex.ja: 彼はもう少しで成功するところだった。

ex.en: She was within an ace of saying "I don't know".
ex.ja: 彼女は危うく「知らない」と言ってしまうところだった。

en: To modify.
To improve or rectify.

adjust.ety: From Middle English ajusten, borrowed from Middle French adjuster, or Old French, from Latin ad (“to, up to, towards”) + iustus (“correct, proper, exact”); Equivalent to ad- + just. Probably influenced in sense by Old French ajouster (cf. modern ajouter), from Vulgar Latin *adiuxtāre, from Latin iuxta. The Middle English originally meant "to correct, remedy" in the late 14th century, and was reborrowed from Middle French in the early 17th century. According to another view on the etymology, the word was actually derived from Old French ajouster and then supposedly later influenced by folk etym

ex.en: They soon adjusted themselves to the new circumstances.
ex.ja: 彼らはすぐにその新しい環境に順応した。

ex.en: She soon adjusted herself to the new school.
ex.ja: 彼女じきに新しい学校に慣れた。

ex.en: She soon adjusted to his way of life.
ex.ja: 彼女はじきに彼の生き方に順応した。

en: Happening by turns; one following the other in succession of time or place; first one and then the other (repeatedly).
Alternating; (of e.g. a pair of tinctures which a charge is coloured) succeeding in turns, or (relative to the field) counterchanged.
That which alternates with something else; vicissitude.
A substitute; an alternative; one designated to take the place of another, if necessary, in performing some duty.
To perform by turns, or in succession; to cause to succeed by turns; to interchange regularly.
To happen, succeed, or act by turns; to follow reciprocally in place or time; followed by with.

alternate.ety: Borrowed from Latin alternātus, the perfect passive participle of Latin alternō (“to take turns”) (see -ate (1,2 and 3)), from alternus (“one after another, by turns”), from alter (“other”) + -nus. Doublet of altern; see also alter.

ex.en: We alternated with each other in driving the car.
ex.ja: 私達は交代で車を運転しました。

ex.en: It was a week of alternating snow and rain.
ex.ja: 雨と雪が交互に降った一週間だった。

ex.en: There are maps on alternate pages of the book.
ex.ja: その本には１ページおきに地図がのっている。

note.ja: alter（他方の）+ nate。一方と他方を代わる代わる →「交互にする・交互の」。

en: The tendency to attract.
The state of being attractive.

ex.en: Do you feel any attraction for this book?
ex.ja: この本に何か魅力感じますか。

ex.en: His attraction lies in his character, not his looks.
ex.ja: 彼の魅力はルックスではなく性格だ。

ex.en: His chief attraction lies in his character, not his looks.
ex.ja: 彼の一番の魅力は容貌にではなく、性格にある。

en: A legally declared or recognized condition of insolvency of a person or organization.
A rule in Tycoon where if the top player does not get first place that round, they instantly get last place

ex.en: Corporate bankruptcies continued at a high level last month.
ex.ja: 企業倒産は先月も高水準に推移した。

ex.ja: その会社は今にも倒産しようとしている。

ex.en: As a matter of fact, bankruptcy is inevitable.
ex.ja: 実際のところ、倒産は避けられない。

en: A generally accepted principle; a rule.
A formally codified set of criteria deemed mandatory for a particular artistic style of figurative art.

canon.ety: From Middle English canoun, from Old French canon and Old English canon, both from Latin canōn, from Ancient Greek κανών (kanṓn, “measuring rod, standard”), akin to κάννα (kánna, “reed”), from Semitic (compare Hebrew קָנֶה (qane, “reed”) and Arabic قَنَاة (qanāh, “reed”)). Doublet of qanun. See also cane, cannon, canyon, canal.

en: The power or ability to generate an outcome.
A digital token allowing a user or process to interact in a specified way with an object that is subject to access control.

capability.ety: Formed in Modern English as capable + -ity.

ex.en: The new team has the capability to win.
ex.ja: 新しいチームには優勝する力がある。

ex.en: It was because she had faith in his capabilities.
ex.ja: というのは彼女が彼の能力を信頼していたからである。

ex.en: She has the wonderful capability to overcome any obstacle.
ex.ja: 彼女はどんな障害をも克服できるすばらしい能力を持っている。

en: An event or occurrence that signifies an ending.
A feeling of completeness; the experience of an emotional conclusion, usually to a difficult period.
To end the parliamentary debate on (an issue) by closure.

closure.ety: From Middle English closure, from Old French closure, from Late Latin clausura, from Latin claudere (“to close”); see clausure and cloture (etymological doublets) and close.

ex.en: The school's closure was due to the snow.
ex.ja: 学校が休みになったのは雪のせいだった。

note.ja: clos（閉じる）+ ure。閉じること →「閉鎖・終結」。

en: A person or organization against whom one is competing.
A participant in a competition, especially in athletics.

competitor.ety: Borrowed from Middle French compétiteur, from Latin competitor.

ex.en: He is superior to his competitors in everything.
ex.ja: 彼は競争相手よりもあらゆる点で優っている。

ex.en: His beating four competitors in a row won our high school team the championship.
ex.ja: 彼の４人抜きの活躍でうちの高校のチームが優勝しました。

ex.en: All the competitors are trying to get their piece of the pie.
ex.ja: すべての競合会社がパイの分け前を得ようとしています。

en: Someone who defends people or property.
One of the players whose primary task is to prevent the opposition from scoring.

defender.ety: From Middle English defender, deffender, defendere, defendour, defendoure, partly from Anglo-Norman defendour, from Old French defendëor; partly from Middle English defenden + -ere, equivalent to defend + -er.

ex.en: The defenders put up a stout resistance.
ex.ja: 防衛者達は強い抵抗を見せた。

Of or concerning dentistry.
Cleaning and polishing of an animal's teeth.
A dental sound.

ex.ja: 歯のクリーニングの費用はいくらですか。

en: Concerning the relationships between the governments of countries.
Exhibiting diplomacy; exercising tact or courtesy; using discussion to avoid hard feelings, fights or arguments.
The science of diplomas, or the art of deciphering ancient writings and determining their age, authenticity, etc.; paleography.

diplomatic.ety: From French diplomatique and its etymon New Latin diplōmaticus. By surface analysis, diplomat + -ic.

ex.en: The two countries do not have diplomatic relations.
ex.ja: その両国は外交関係がない。

ex.en: Japan has diplomatic relations with China.
ex.ja: 日本は中国と外交関係がある。

ex.en: Tom is diplomatic, but Mary isn't.
ex.ja: トムは外交的だけど、メアリーはそうでもない。

en: A percussive musical instrument spanned with a thin covering on at least one end for striking, forming an acoustic chamber; a membranophone.
Any similar hollow, cylindrical object.
To beat a drum.
To beat with a rapid succession of strokes.

drum.ety:
Perhaps back-formation from drumslade (“drummer”), from Middle Dutch trommelslach (“drumbeat”), from trommel (“drum”) + slach (“beat”) (Dutch slag).
Or perhaps borrowed directly from a continental Germanic language; compare Middle Dutch tromme (“drum”), Middle Low German trumme (“drum”) et al. Compare also Middle High German trumme, trumbe (“drum”), Old High German trumba (“trumpet”). Compare Ancient Greek τῠ́μπᾰνον (tŭ́mpănon, “kettledrum”) whence Modern English timbre.

ex.en: Tom has been beating the drum for the project.
ex.ja: トムはそのプロジェクトをずいぶん宣伝しているよ。

ex.en: She drummed her fingers on the table.
ex.ja: 彼女は指でテーブルをとんとんたたいた。

ex.en: A boy was beating the drum.
ex.ja: 少年がその太鼓を叩いていた。

en: Of or relating to an editor, editing or an editorial.
Appropriate for high fashion magazines.
An article in a publication giving the opinion of its editors on a given topic or current event.
A similar commentary on radio or television.

ex.ja: 彼らは反植民地主義的な社説で党を全面的に支持した。

en: To amuse (someone); to engage the attention of agreeably.
To have someone over at one's home, or some other venue, for a party or visit.

entertain.ety:
From Middle English entertenen, from Middle French entretenir, from Old French entretenir, from entre (“among”) + tenir (“to hold”), from Latin inter + teneō (“hold, keep”). For the noun, compare French entretien.
Sense of answering a phone call in Malaysian English is influenced by Malay layan “to serve, to attend to or engage with something”.

ex.en: Intended for children, the book entertains grown-ups.
ex.ja: 子供向けに書かれているが、この本は大人も楽しませる。

ex.en: They gave a play to entertain their teachers.
ex.ja: 彼らは先生を楽しませるために劇をした。

ex.en: He often entertained his friends over the weekend.
ex.ja: 彼はよく友人達を週末に家に招いてもてなした。

note.ja: enter（= inter 間に）+ tain（保つ）。人々の間を保つ →（客をもてなして間をもたせる）→「楽しませる・もてなす」。

en: Lasting forever; unending.
Existing outside time; as opposed to sempiternal, existing within time but everlastingly.
One who lives forever; an immortal.

eternal.ety: From Middle English eternal, from Old French eternal, from Late Latin aeternālis, from Latin aeternus (“eternal”), from aevum (“age”). Displaced native Old English ēċe.

ex.en: Some people believe in eternal life after death.
ex.ja: 死後の永遠の生命を信じている人もいる。

ex.en: Keep in mind that youth is not eternal.
ex.ja: 若さは永遠ではないということを忘れてはならない。

ex.en: Let us pray for a perfect, an eternal, peace.
ex.ja: 完璧な平和を。 永遠なる平和を祈ろう。

en: Very broad; pertaining or appropriate to large classes or groups as opposed to specific instances.
Lacking in precision, often in an evasive fashion; vague; imprecise.
A product sold under a generic name.
A wine that is a combination of several wines, or made from a combination of several grape varieties.

generic.ety: From Middle French générique, from Latin genus (“genus, kind”) + -ic.

note.ja: ラテン語 genus（種類）から。種類全体の →「一般的な・ノーブランドの」。

en: Grandmother.
Any elderly woman, regardless of if she has grandchildren.

ex.en: My grandma injured her leg in a fall.
ex.ja: おばあちゃんが転んで、足にけがをしちゃったんです。

ex.en: She's not my grandma; she's my mom.
ex.ja: 彼女は私のお婆ちゃんじゃなくてママです。

ex.en: My grandma still calls me "Little Hide."
ex.ja: うちのおばあちゃんってさ、今でも俺のこと「秀ちゃん」っていうんだ。

en: To take hold (of), particularly with the hand.
To figuratively take hold of or grasp.
A hold or way of holding, particularly with the hand.
Ability to resist slippage when pressed in contact with another object or surface.

grip.ety:
Verb from Middle English grippen, from Old English grippan, from a Proto-Germanic *gripjaną (compare Old High German gripfen); compare the related Old English grīpan, whence English gripe. See also grope, and the related Proto-Germanic *grīpaną.
Noun from Middle English grippe, gripe, an amalgam of Old English gripe (“grasp, hold”) (cognate with German Griff) and Old English gripa (“handful”) (cognate with Swedish grepp).

ex.en: He was in the grip of poverty.
ex.ja: 彼は貧乏にとりつかれていた。

ex.en: Tom got a grip on his emotions.
ex.ja: トムは自分の感情をぐっと抑えた。

ex.en: I have a gripping pain here.
ex.ja: ここが差し込むように痛みます。

en: The amount that a hand will grasp or contain.
A small number, usually approximately five.

handful.ety: From Middle English handful, hondful, from Old English handfull (“handful”), from Proto-Germanic *handufullō, *handufulliz (“handful”), from Proto-Germanic *handuz (“hand”) + *fullaz (“full”); equivalent to hand + full (“fullness, plenty”) or hand + -ful. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Hondful (“handful”), West Frisian hânfol (“handful”), Dutch handvol (“handful”), German Handvoll (“handful”), Danish håndfuld (“handful”), Swedish handfull (“handful”), Icelandic handfylli (“handful”).

ex.en: Only a handful of people know the fact.
ex.ja: ほんの少数の人しかその事実を知らない。

ex.en: Only a handful of people came to the meeting.
ex.ja: 会合にはほんのわずかの人しか出てこなかった。

ex.en: That boy is a handful.
ex.ja: あの子は手がかかる。

en: In a happy or cheerful manner; with happiness.
By good chance; fortunately, successfully.

happily.ety: From Middle English happily, happyly, happyliche, happylyche, equivalent to happy + -ly.

ex.en: We must keep the law to live happily.
ex.ja: 私たちは幸せに生きるために法律を守らなければならない。

ex.en: I want to happily fall in love.
ex.ja: 幸せな恋愛がしたい。

ex.en: I will happily do it.
ex.ja: 私でよければ喜んで。

en: Agreement or accord.
A pleasing combination of elements, or arrangement of sounds.

ex.ja: 彼の家の前には松の木が立っている。

ex.en: This is a well-shaped pine tree.
ex.ja: これは格好のよい松の木だ。

ex.en: Tall pine trees form a ring around the lake.
ex.ja: 高い松の木が湖の周囲を取り囲んでいる。

en: To place in an attitude or fixed position, for the sake of effect.
To ask; to set (a test, quiz, riddle, etc.).
Position, posture, arrangement (especially of the human body).
Affectation.

pose.ety: From Middle English pose, from Old English ġeposu pl (“cold in the head; catarrh”, literally “(the) sneezes; (the) snorts”), from Old English pos, ġepos (“sneeze, snort”), from Proto-West Germanic *pos, from Proto-Germanic *pusą (“sneeze, snort”), from Proto-Germanic *pusōną, *pusjaną (“to snort, blow”), from *pus- (“to blow, breathe hard”), from Proto-Indo-European *bew- (“to blow, swell”). Compare Low German pusten (“to blow, puff”), German dialectal pfausen (“to sneeze, snort”), Norwegian dialectal pysa (“to blow”).

ex.en: He posed as my close friend.
ex.ja: 彼はいかにも私の親友らしく見せかけた。

ex.en: Tom was posing as a doctor.
ex.ja: トムは医者を装っていた。

ex.en: He posed as a dentist at that bar.
ex.ja: 彼はその酒場で歯医者に成りすましていた。

note.ja: ラテン語 pausare（止まる）から（後に ponere「置く」と混同された）。ある姿勢で止まる →「ポーズ（をとる）・（問題を）提起する」。

en: To cause (liquid, or liquid-like substance) to flow in a stream, either out of a container or into it.
To send out as in a stream or a flood; to cause (an emotion) to come out; to cause to escape.
The act of pouring.
Something, or an amount, poured.

pour.ety:
From Middle English pouren (“to pour”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Old Northern French purer (“to sift (grain), pour out (water)”), from Latin pūrō (“to purify”), from pūrus (“pure”). Compare Middle Dutch afpuren (“to pour off, drain”).
To pour displaced several Middle English verbs:
* schenchen, schenken (“to pour”), from Old English sċenċan (“to pour out”) and Old Norse skenkja, from Proto-Germanic *skankijaną. Compare dialectal English shink, skink.
* yeten, from Old English ġēotan (“to pour”), from Proto-Germanic *geutaną.
* birlen (“to pour, serve drink to”), from Old English byrel

ex.en: The excited crowd poured out of the stadium.
ex.ja: 興奮した群衆が競技場から溢れ出てきた。

ex.en: She poured a cup of tea for me.
ex.ja: 彼女は私にお茶を１杯入れてくれた。

ex.en: Words of abuse poured from his lips.
ex.ja: ののしりの言葉が彼の口をついて出てきた。

en: To issue (something, such as printed work) for distribution and/or sale.
To announce to the public.

publish.ety: From Middle English publicen (by analogy with banish, finish), from Old French publier, from Latin publicare (“to make public, show or tell to the people, make known, declare, also (and earlier) confiscate for public use”), from publicus (“pertaining to the people, public”); see public.

ex.en: Professor White published his first book last year.
ex.ja: ホワイト教授は去年処女作を出版した。

ex.en: The magazine Look is no longer being published.
ex.ja: Ｌｏｏｋは廃刊になった。

ex.en: When is that novel going to be published?
ex.ja: その小説はいつ出版されるの？

note.ja: ラテン語 publicare（公にする）から。publ（人々の）。人々に公開する →「出版する・公表する」。

The payment made to rent something.
Relating to rent.
Relating to renting.

In a seemly manner; decorously; with propriety.

ex.en: It is severely cold this winter.
ex.ja: 今年の冬は寒さが厳しいですね。

en: Any predatory fish of the superorder Selachimorpha, with a cartilaginous skeleton and 5 to 7 gill slits on each side of its head.
Meat of this animal, consumed as food.

shark.ety:
From Middle English shark (used by Thomas Beckington in 1442 to refer to a kind of fish), of uncertain origin. Most likely from a semantic extension of the German-derived shark (“scoundrel”), see below. The fish was originally called a dogfish or haye in English and Middle English. Its name in Old English is unknown, although some uses of the word hranfisċ that do not appear to carry the sense of "whale" may have been referencing it.

ex.en: Tom caught a shark.
ex.ja: トムはサメを捕まえた。

ex.en: My older brother borrowed money from a loan shark.
ex.ja: 兄が高利貸しに借金したんです。

ex.en: According to the news, he was eaten by sharks.
ex.ja: ニュースによると彼はサメに食べられたということだ。

en: The intercardinal compass point halfway between south and west; specifically at a bearing of 225°.
Of, in or pertaining to the southwest; southwestern.
Situated toward or in the direction of the southwest; southwestward; southwesterly.
Towards or in the direction of the southwest; southwestwards.

southwest.ety: From Middle English southwest, southewest, from Old English sūþwest and sūþanwestan, equivalent to south + west. Cognate with West Frisian súdwest, Dutch zuidwest, German Südwesten, Danish sydvest, Swedish sydväst.

A person who is able to endure hardship.

ex.ja: その墜落事故の唯一の生存者は赤ちゃんだった。

Based on formal (de jure) arguments, which, however, may be misleading.

en: Limitless or without bounds; unrestricted.

unlimited.ety: From Middle English unlimitid, equivalent to un- + limited.

Having a feeling of anxiety or disquietude; extremely concerned, especially about something that will happen in the future or that is unk…

ex.ja: クリスはとても大学に行きたがっている。

ex.en: Turn left and you will find the cafe.
ex.ja: 左へ曲がれば、喫茶店が見つかるでしょう。

ex.ja: タバコを吸ってもいいですか？

ex.en: How many cigarettes do you smoke per day?
ex.ja: タバコを１日何本吸いますか？

ex.en: Someone left a burning cigarette on the table.
ex.ja: 誰かがこのテーブルに火が付いたままのタバコをおきっぱなしにしました。

en: The veneration, devotion, and religious rites given to a deity (especially in a historical polytheistic context), or (in a Christian cont…
A group of people having an obsession with or intense admiration for a particular activity, idea, person or thing.
Of or relating to a cult.
Enjoyed by a small, loyal group.

cult.ety: Derived from French culte, from Latin cultus (“care, adoration; cult”), from colō (“cultivate; protect”).

ex.ja: トムがカルト集団に入ったって、本当？

ex.en: Is it true Tom joined a cult?
ex.ja: トムがカルト集団に入ったって、本当？

ex.en: What's the difference between a religion and a cult?
ex.ja: 宗教とカルトの違いは何ですか？

note.ja: ラテン語 cultus（崇拝・耕作）から。cult（耕す・あがめる）。→「崇拝・カルト」。culture と同じ語源。

en: (also dairy products or dairy produce) Products produced from milk.
A place, often on a farm, where milk is processed and turned into products such as butter and cheese.
Referring to products produced from milk.
Referring to products produced from animal milk as opposed to non-milk substitutes.

dairy.ety: Inherited from Middle English deyerie (“dairy, dairy farm”), from Anglo-Norman deyerie (“dairy”), from deye (“dairymaid”) + -erie (“-ery”); by surface analysis, dey (“dairymaid”) + -ry. Cognate with Scots dery, dyrie.

ex.en: I really hate dairy products.
ex.ja: 私は本当に乳製品が嫌いです。

ex.en: A dairy cow is a useful animal.
ex.ja: 乳牛というのは、役に立つ動物です。

ex.en: I seldom eat dairy products.
ex.ja: 乳製品はめったに食べません。

en: Often used as an affectionate term of address: a person who is very dear to one.
A person who is kind, sweet, etc., and thus lovable; a pet, a sweetheart; also, an animal or thing which is cute and lovable.
Very dear; beloved, cherished, favourite.
Very cute or lovable; adorable, charming, sweet.
To call (someone) "darling" (noun sense 1).

darling.ety: The noun is derived from Middle English dereling, derelyng (“beloved person; beloved of God, devout Christian”), from Old English dīerling, dēorling (“favourite, darling; minion”), from Proto-West Germanic *diuriling, from Proto-Germanic *diurijalingaz, from *diurijaz (“beloved, dear; expensive”) (further etymology uncertain, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *dʰegʷʰ- (“hot, warm; to burn”), or *dweh₂- (“distant, long; to remove, separate”)) + *-ilingaz (suffix forming (diminutive) nouns with the sense of ‘belonging to; coming from’). By surface analysis, dear + -ling (suffix meaning ‘immature

ex.en: What are you doing, darling?
ex.ja: 何をしているの、ダーリン？

ex.en: Let's dance, my darling.
ex.ja: ねぇ、あなた、踊りましょう。

ex.en: I call my sweetheart darling.
ex.ja: 私は恋人を「ダーリン」と呼びます。

en: Joy; pleasure.
Something that gives great joy or pleasure.
To give delight to; to affect with great pleasure; to please highly.
To have or take great pleasure.

delight.ety: Attested from the 13th century, from Middle English delite, from Old French deleiter, deliter, from Latin dēlectāre (“to delight, please”), frequentative of dēlicere (“to allure, entice”), from dē- (“away”) + laciō (“to lure, to deceive”), from Proto-Italic *lakjō (“to draw, pull”), of unknown ultimate origin. Doublet of delect. Related with delectation, delicate, delicious and dilettante. The modern unetymological spelling (instead of expected delite) is influenced by light and other words ending in -ight, such as might, bright, etc. The -gh- may also be an attempt to represent the Latin -c-;

ex.en: We were delighted to hear of your success.
ex.ja: 私たちはあなたの成功を聞いてうれしかった。

ex.en: I am delighted to have met you today.
ex.ja: 今日、あなたとあえて、とっても嬉しいな。

ex.en: I read your new book with real delight.
ex.ja: 新しい本を本当に大喜びで読ませていただきました。

en: A daily log of experiences, especially those of the writer.
A personal organizer or appointment diary.
To keep a diary or journal.

diary.ety: From Latin diārium (“a daily allowance for soldiers, in Late Latin also ‘diary’”), neuter of *diārius, from diēs (“a day”) (whence also journal). Cognate with Spanish diario (“daily; diary”).

ex.en: I wrote a lot in my diary yesterday.
ex.ja: 昨日は私は日記にたくさん書きました。

ex.en: I've decided to keep a diary this year.
ex.ja: 今年は日記をつけようと決心した。

ex.en: I've been keeping a diary for three years.
ex.ja: 三年間日記を付け続けたのよ。

en: To fail to agree; to have a different opinion or belief.
To fail to conform or correspond with.

disagree.ety: From Middle English disagre (“to refuse to assent to”), from Anglo-Norman disagreer, disagrer, desagreer (“to refuse assent”), from Old French desagreer, desagrëer (“to be disagreeable; to be unpleasant”) (modern French désagréer (“to displease”)); the English word is analysable as dis- + agree.

ex.en: This is where we absolutely disagree with you.
ex.ja: この点で私達はまったくあなたと意見が違います。

ex.en: This is where I absolutely disagree with you.
ex.ja: この点では、私は全くあなたと意見が違う。

ex.en: This is the reason I disagree with you.
ex.ja: こういうわけで私はあなたに反対なのです。

en: To create (a hole) by removing material with a drill (tool).
To practice, especially in (or as in) a military context.
A tool or machine used to remove material so as to create a hole, typically by plunging a rotating cutting bit into a stationary workpiece.
The portion of a drilling tool that drives the bit.

drill.ety: From Middle Dutch drillen (“bore, move in a circle”).

ex.ja: 今日、学校で避難訓練をしました。

ex.ja: 私たちは昨日防火訓練をした。

ex.en: They intended to drill for oil.
ex.ja: 彼らは穴をあけて石油を掘り当てようとした。

en: The currency unit of the European Monetary Union. Symbol: €
A coin with a face value of one euro.

euro.ety: The name euro was the winner of a contest open to the general public to propose names for the new European currency, and as such is technically a neologism, although it obviously alludes to the common root of geographical names for the continent Europe, derived from Latin Europa, from Ancient Greek Εὐρώπη (Eurṓpē), the name in Greek mythology of a princess, abducted by Zeus as a bull across the Bosporus. According to the official story, the term was coined by Belgian teacher and esperantist Germain Pirlot in 1995, who suggested it in a letter to Jacques Santer, then President of the European C

ex.en: How much is 300 euros in U.S. dollars?
ex.ja: 300ユーロって、アメリカドルでいくらなの？

ex.en: I don't remember exactly, but I spent over 1000 euros.
ex.ja: 正確には覚えてないんだけど、1,000ユーロ以上使ったよ。

ex.en: They cost three Euros a piece.
ex.ja: 1つ3ユーロです。

en: To estimate how something will be in the future.
To foreshadow; to suggest something in advance.
An estimation of a future condition.
A prediction of the weather.

forecast.ety:
From Middle English forecasten, forcasten, equivalent to fore- + cast.
The noun is from Middle English forecast, forcast.

ex.en: According to the weather forecast, it'll rain tomorrow.
ex.ja: 天気予報によると、明日は雨だそうだ。

ex.en: According to the weather forecast, it'll snow tomorrow.
ex.ja: 天気予報によればあすは雪だ。

ex.en: The weather forecast said it's going to rain.
ex.ja: 天気予報だと、雨が降るって。

en: The process, or the power, of governing; government or administration.
The specific system by which a political system is ruled.

governance.ety: From Middle English governaunce, from Old French gouvernance, governance, equivalent to govern + -ance.

ex.en: Corporate governance and accountability are being strengthened.
ex.ja: コーポレートガバナンスや説明責任を強化している。

en: A close embrace, especially when charged with an emotion such as affection, joy, relief, lust, anger, aggression, compassion, or the like…
A particular grip in wrestling.
To cling closely together.
To embrace by holding closely, especially in the arms.

hug.ety: From earlier hugge (“to embrace, clasp with the arms”) (1560), probably representing a conflation of huck (“to crouch, huddle down”) and Old Norse hugga (“to comfort, console”), from hugr (“mind, heart, thought”), from Proto-Germanic *hugiz (“mind, thought, sense”), cognate with Icelandic hugga (“to comfort”), Old English hyġe (“thought”) (whence high (Etymology 2)).

ex.en: Tom and Mary are hugging each other naked.
ex.ja: トムとメアリーは生まれたままの姿で抱き合っている。

ex.en: Would it be OK if I hugged you?
ex.ja: 抱き締めてもいいですか？

ex.en: When I finished reading that book, I hugged it.
ex.ja: その本を読み終えると、私は本をぎゅっと抱きしめた。

en: Situated in, or designed to be used in, or carried on within, the interior of a building.

ex.en: The world's largest indoor beach is located in Brandenburg, Germany.
ex.ja: 世界一の大きさを誇る室内ビーチは、ドイツのブランデンブルクにあります。

ex.en: Nancy enjoys indoor games.
ex.ja: ナンシーは屋内競技が好きです。

en: Having or exerting influence.
A person who has influence

influential.ety: From Medieval Latin īnfluentiālis, from īnfluentia + -ālis. By surface analysis, influence + -ial.

ex.en: I'm not as influential as you think I am.
ex.ja: あなたが思っているほど私は影響力がない。

ex.en: He's very influential in Kansai's adult industry.
ex.ja: 彼は関西のアダルト産業に強い影響力を持っている。

en: Unable to be seen; out of sight; not visible.
Not appearing on the surface.
To make invisible, to invisiblize.

invisible.ety:
From Middle English invisible, from Old French invisible, from Late Latin invīsibilis. Displaced native Old English unġesewenlīċ.
Morphologically in- + visible. Piecewise doublet of unvisible.

ex.en: Tom said he saw the invisible man today.
ex.ja: トムが今日透明人間を見たんだって。

ex.en: Tom said that he saw the invisible man today.
ex.ja: トムが今日透明人間を見たんだって。

ex.en: Can you see the invisible man?
ex.ja: 透明人間が見えますか？

en: A pair of trousers made from denim cotton.

jeans.ety: From Gene(s) (also spelled Jean(s)), an obsolete English name for the Italian city of Genoa. Compare French Gênes. In the context of clothing, the term originally denoted a kind of coarse cotton (known more fully as Gene(s) fustian) that was associated with Genoa. It began to be used for trousers made of such cloth in the 19th century. At this point, the final -s was reanalysed as a plural ending.

ex.en: When Peter got up, Jean had already left home.
ex.ja: ピーターが起きたときには、ジーンはすでに家を出ていた。

ex.en: I'd like to talk to Jean.
ex.ja: 僕はジーンと話したい。

ex.en: Made in Italy, these jeans were very expensive.
ex.ja: イタリー製なので、このジーンズはとても値段が高かった。

en: In civil law, a case where two or more people disagree and one or more of the parties take the case to a court for resolution.
To bring a lawsuit.

ex.en: I would prefer any alternative to a lawsuit.
ex.ja: 私は訴訟に変わるものがあればなんでもいい。

ex.en: The lawsuit is likely to end in our defeat.
ex.ja: 裁判はこちらの負けにおわりそうだ。

ex.en: The lawsuit remains undecided.
ex.ja: 訴訟は未決である。

en: A crack, crevice, fissure, or hole which admits water or other fluid, or lets it escape.
The entrance or escape of a fluid through a crack, fissure, or other aperture.
To allow fluid or gas to pass through an opening that should be sealed.
(of a fluid or gas) To pass through an opening that should be sealed.

leak.ety:
From Middle English leken (“to let water in or out”), from Old English *lecan (“to leak”), Middle Dutch leken (“to leak, drip”) or Old Norse leka (“to leak, drip”); all from Proto-Germanic *lekaną (“to leak, drain”), from Proto-Indo-European *leg- (“to leak”).
Cognate with Dutch lekken (“to leak”), German lechen, lecken (“to leak”), Danish lække (“to leak”), Swedish läcka (“to leak”), Norwegian Bokmål lekke (“to leak”), Faroese, Icelandic, and Norwegian Nynorsk leka (“to leak”). Related also to Old English leċċan (“to water, wet”), Albanian lag, lak (“to damp, make wet”). See also leach, lake.

ex.en: Tom is taking a leak behind the house.
ex.ja: トムは家の後ろでおしっこしてるんだ。

ex.en: The leak needs to be stopped immediately.
ex.ja: 漏えいはすぐに食いとめる必要がある。

ex.en: The information seems to have leaked out.
ex.ja: 情報が外部に漏れたらしい。

en: A composer, conductor, or performer of music; specifically, a person who sings and/or plays a musical instrument as a hobby, occupation, …

musician.ety: From Middle English musician, musicien, from Old French musicien (“musician”), equivalent to musike + -ien. By surface analysis, music + -ician.

ex.en: Are there any famous musicians on the stage?
ex.ja: 舞台には有名な音楽家がいますか。

ex.en: I am the first musician in my family.
ex.ja: 私は家族の中で初めての音楽家なのです。

ex.en: He is a musician of the first rank.
ex.ja: 彼は一流の音楽家だ。

en: A tree of species Olea europaea cultivated since ancient times in the Mediterranean for its fruit and the oil obtained from it.
The small oval fruit of this tree, eaten ripe (usually black) or unripe (usually green).
Of a grayish green color, that of an unripe olive.

olive.ety: From Middle English olyve, from Old French olive (“olive, olive tree”), from Latin olīva (“olive”), itself from either Etruscan *𐌄𐌋𐌄𐌉𐌅𐌀 (*eleiva), Proto-Hellenic *elaíwā (compare Mycenaean Greek 𐀁𐀨𐀷 (e-ra-wa), Ancient Greek ἐλαίᾱ (elaíā)), or the same source as those two. In any case, ultimately from a Mediterranean Pre-Greek source, possibly Proto-Berber *wlw (“wild olive”). More questionably, maybe from Proto-Indo-European *loiwom (compare Old Church Slavonic лои (loi, “tallow”), Old Armenian եւղ (ewł, “oil”)). Doublet of oliva and oil. Displaced native Old English eleberġe, literally "oil b

ex.en: I'd rather use olive oil than butter.
ex.ja: バターを使うよりオリーブオイルの方がいいな。

ex.en: We'd like to order 18 tonnes of olive oil.
ex.ja: オリーブオイルを１８ＭＴ注文します。

ex.en: You like olives, don't you?
ex.ja: オリーブが好きなんだよね？

en: Given to strong feeling, sometimes romantic, sexual, or both.
Fired with intense feeling.

passionate.ety: From Middle English passionat, from Medieval Latin passiōnātus (“affected, impassioned, libidinous, easely angered”). Equivalent to passion + -ate (adjective-forming suffix). Compare French passionné.

ex.en: She had a passionate interest in music.
ex.ja: 彼女は音楽を熱烈に愛好していた。

ex.en: So passionate was his letter that she was moved to tears.
ex.ja: 彼の手紙がとても情熱的だったので彼女は感動して涙がでできた。

ex.en: Tom is passionate about music.
ex.ja: トムは、音楽に情熱を注いでいます。

en: An official whose job is to receive taxes or other monies; a tax collector, a treasurer.
A person who receives something in a general sense; a recipient.

receiver.ety: Inherited from Middle English receyvour, from Anglo-Norman receverre, receivour et al., later also reformed as receive + -er. Compare recevor, rescaivour.

ex.en: I put the receiver to my ear.
ex.ja: 私は受話器を耳に当てた。

ex.en: He took up the receiver and dialed.
ex.ja: 彼は受話器を取り上げてダイアルを回した。

ex.en: I forgot to lift the receiver before dialing the number.
ex.ja: ぼくはうっかり受話器をはずさないでダイヤルを回した。

en: A tumultuous disturbance of the public peace by a large group of people, often involving violence or damage to property.
A wide and unconstrained variety.
To create or take part in a riot; to raise an uproar or sedition.
To cause to riot; to throw into a tumult.

riot.ety:
From Middle English riot (“debauched living, dissipation”), from Old French riote (“debate”), from rioter (“to quarrel”), perhaps related to riboter or from Latin rugio (“to roar”).
Compare French riotte and Occitan riòta.

ex.en: The riot was soon put down by the police.
ex.ja: その暴動はすぐに警察によって鎮圧された。

ex.en: The garden was a riot of color.
ex.ja: 庭には様々な花が咲き乱れていた。

ex.en: The riot police arrived on the scene.
ex.ja: 機動隊が現場に到着した。

en: A list of individuals or groups, usually for an organization of some kind such as military officers and enlisted personnel enrolled in a …
A list of the jobs to be performed by members of an organization and often with the date and time that they are expected to perform them.
To place the name of (a person) on a roster.
To show the elements of a set by listing them inside brackets.

roster.ety: Borrowed from Dutch rooster (“gridiron, table, list”), from Middle Dutch roosten (“to roast”). More at roast.

en: One who is hired to perform regular household or other duties, and receives compensation. As opposed to a slave.
One who serves another, providing help in some manner.

servant.ety: From Middle English servaunt, from Old French servant, from the present participle of the verb servir. Doublet of sergeant and servient. Morphologically serve + -ant. Displaced native Old English þeġn.

ex.en: He got angry and told off his servant.
ex.ja: 彼は怒って召し使いを叱った。

ex.en: He had three servants to wait on him.
ex.ja: 彼には彼に仕える召し使いが３人いた。

ex.en: He was a kind master to his servants.
ex.ja: 彼は使用人に優しい雇い主だった。

en: Equipment designed for a particular purpose; an apparatus.
The fashion in which something is organized or arranged.
The main bones of the head considered as a unit; including the cranium, facial bones, and mandible.
These bones as a symbol for death; death's-head.
To hit in the head with a fist, a weapon, or a thrown object.
To strike the top of (the ball).

skull.ety:
From Middle English sculle, scolle (also schulle, scholle), probably from a dialectal form of Old Norse skalli (“bald head, skull”), itself probably related to Old English sċealu (“husk”), to Proto-Norse *ᛋᚲᚨᛚᛟ (*skalo), from Proto-Germanic *skallô; compare Finnish kallo. Compare Scots scull, Danish skal (“skull”) and skalle (“bald head, skull”), Norwegian skalle, Swedish skalle and especially dialectal Swedish skulle.
Related to Old Norse skoltr (“brow”), skolptr (“muzzle, snout”), akin to Icelandic skoltur (“jaw”), dialectal Swedish skult, skulle (“dome, crown of the head, skull”), Norwegian

ex.en: Closer examination revealed that the skull had been crushed by some heavy blow.
ex.ja: 調べを進めるうちに、頭蓋骨が、何か重い一撃を受けて打ち砕かれているのが明らかになった。

en: The sound of a violent impact; a violent striking together.
A traffic collision.
To break (something brittle) violently.
To be destroyed by being smashed.

smash.ety: Uncertain, probably of onomatopoeic origin. Compare Swedish smask (“to smack with the lips”), dialectal Swedish smaska (“to smack, kiss”), Danish smaske (“to smack with the lips”), Low German smaksen (“to smack with the lips, kiss”).

ex.en: Who smashed the window? Tell me the truth.
ex.ja: 誰が窓を割ったの？本当のことを言いなさい。

ex.en: There was a smash-up out on Route 66 today.
ex.ja: 今日ルート６６で衝突事故があったんだ。

ex.en: The bottle smashed to pieces.
ex.ja: 瓶は粉々に割れた。

en: A three-dimensional work of art, usually representing a person or animal, usually created by sculpting, carving, molding, or casting.
To form a statue of; to make into a statue.

statue.ety: From Old French statue, from Latin statua, derived from statuō (“set up or erect”). Doublet of statua.

ex.en: He was as still as a statue.
ex.ja: 彼は彫像のようにじっとしていた。

ex.en: This statue is as large as life.
ex.ja: この像は実物大です。

ex.en: We must move this statue very carefully.
ex.ja: 私たちは十分注意してこの彫像を動かさなければならない。

note.ja: ラテン語 statua（立てられたもの）から。sta（立つ）。立っている像 →「像・彫像」。

en: In a way that causes surprise because it is unexpected, or unusual.

surprisingly.ety:
Etymology tree
English surprising
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English surprisingly
From surprising + -ly.

ex.en: Tom always gets the job done surprisingly fast.
ex.ja: トムはいつも驚くほど仕事が早い。

ex.en: It's a surprisingly large room, isn't it?
ex.ja: 意外とでかい部屋なんだね。

ex.en: This book is surprisingly easy to read, isn't it?
ex.ja: 案外、この本は読みやすいね。

en: To give up into the power, control, or possession of another.
To yield (a town, a fortification, etc.) to an enemy.
An act of surrendering, submission into the possession of another; a feeling of abandonment and resignation; the deliberate cessation of …
The yielding or delivery of a possession in response to a demand.

surrender.ety: From Middle English surrendren, from Old French surrendre, from sur- + rendre (“render”). Displaced native Old English on hand gān.

ex.en: If I had to surrender, I'd rather choose death.
ex.ja: 降伏するくらいなら死を選びます。

ex.en: The soldiers were told never to surrender.
ex.ja: 兵士たちは決して降伏しないように言われた。

ex.en: Under the circumstances we have no choice but to surrender.
ex.ja: 現状では、私たちは降参するしかない。

en: Arousing suspicion.
Distrustful or tending to suspect.

suspicious.ety: From Old French sospecious, from Latin suspiciosus, suspitiosus.

ex.en: If you see anything suspicious, please contact us.
ex.ja: 不審物を見かけたら、ご連絡ください。

ex.en: The police are suspicious of the old man.
ex.ja: 警察はその老人を疑っている。

ex.en: The way she spoke to us was suspicious.
ex.ja: 彼女の私達への口のきき方は疑い深げだった。

note.ja: su（下から）+ spic（見る）+ ious。下から疑いの目で見る →「疑わしい・疑い深い」。suspect（疑う）。

ex.en: Teenagers want to be independent of their parents.
ex.ja: 十代の子供たちは親から独立したいと思っている。

ex.en: A teenager sometimes acts like a baby.
ex.ja: ティーンエイジャーはたまに赤ん坊のような行動をとる。

ex.en: The report revealed that many teenagers are alcoholics.
ex.ja: その報告書から１０代の多くの子供がアルコール中毒にかかっていることが分かった。

en: Sensitive or painful to the touch.
Easily bruised or injured; not firm or hard; delicate.
The inner flight muscle (pectoralis minor) of poultry.
tenderly
To work on a tender.

tender.ety: From Middle English tender, tendere, from Anglo-Norman tendre, Old French tendre, from Latin tener, tenerum (“soft, delicate”).

ex.en: Tom passed away at the tender age of 30.
ex.ja: トムは享年３０という若さでこの世を去った。

ex.en: His voice was full of tender concern.
ex.ja: 彼の声には優しい気づかいが満ちていた。

ex.en: She gave him a tender kiss.
ex.ja: 彼女は彼に優しくキスをした。

en: In a thorough or complete manner.

ex.en: We went over the house thoroughly before buying it.
ex.ja: その家を徹底的に調べてから購入した。

ex.en: I will email you after I check it thoroughly.
ex.ja: 後でちゃんと調べてメールするわ。

ex.en: He is thoroughly familiar with the business.
ex.ja: 彼はその仕事に精通している。

en: A region of space that contains no matter.
The condition of rarefaction, or reduction of pressure below that of the atmosphere, in a vessel, such as the condenser of a steam engine…
To clean (something) with a vacuum cleaner.
To use a vacuum cleaner.

vacuum.ety:
Borrowed from New Latin vacuum (“vacuum”), a subsense of Classical Latin vacuum (“empty space”), a substantivised form of vacuus (“empty”); related to vacāre (“to be empty”).
The exercise sense comes from analogy to the sucking action of a vacuum cleaner.

ex.en: For that experiment they need a complete vacuum.
ex.ja: その実験には真空が必要だ。

ex.en: His death has left a vacuum in their lives.
ex.ja: 彼の死は彼らの生活に空しさをもたらした。

ex.en: I've been vacuuming the rooms all morning.
ex.ja: 私は午前中ずっと部屋の掃除をしている。

note.ja: ラテン語 vacuus（空の）から。vac（空）。空っぽの空間 →「真空・電気掃除機（で掃除する）」。

en: The act of varying; a partial change in the form, position, state, or qualities of a thing.
A related but distinct thing.

variation.ety: From Middle French variation, from Old French variacion, from Latin variātiō, from vary + -ation.

ex.en: Obviously there are many variations between these two extremes.
ex.ja: むろん、この両極端の間に多くのバリエーションがある。

ex.en: The reason for this is that we found no variation of those morphemes.
ex.ja: このことの理由は、それらの形態素に変異形がまったく見出されなかったからである。

en: An assertion, especially an accusation, not necessarily based on facts.
The act of alleging.

allegation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French allégation, from Latin allegatio, from allegare. By surface analysis, allege + -ation, see allege.

en: To act before (someone), especially to prevent an action.
To take up or introduce (something) prematurely.

anticipate.ety: Borrowed from Latin anticipātus, perfect passive participle of anticipō (“to anticipate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from ante- (“before”), + capiō (“to take”, cip- when prefixed) + -ō (verb-forming suffix). See capable.

ex.en: He anticipates that he will be in trouble.
ex.ja: 彼は困ったことになるだろうと予想している。

ex.en: I anticipated a quiet vacation in the mountains.
ex.ja: 山で静かな休日を過ごせるものと楽しみにしていた。

ex.en: We didn't anticipate their buying a new car.
ex.ja: 私たちは彼らが新車を買うなんて予想もしなかった。

note.ja: anti（= ante 前に）+ cip（取る）+ ate。前もって取る →「予期する・先回りする」。

en: A professional who designs buildings or other structures, or who prepares plans and superintends construction.
A person who plans, devises or contrives the achievement of a desired result.
To design, plan, or orchestrate.

architect.ety: From Middle French architecte, from Latin architectus, from Ancient Greek ἀρχιτέκτων (arkhitéktōn, “master builder”), from ἀρχι- (arkhi-, “chief”) + τέκτων (téktōn, “builder”). By surface analysis, archi- + -tect.

ex.en: The hotel was designed by a Japanese architect.
ex.ja: そのホテルは日本人の建築家によって設計された。

ex.en: Tom has a brother who is an architect.
ex.ja: トムには建築家の弟がいる。

ex.en: Tom was the architect that designed that building.
ex.ja: トムは建築士で、あの建物の設計をした。

en: A wide bowl for washing, sometimes affixed to a wall.
A depression, natural or artificial, containing water.
To create a concavity or depression in.
To serve as or become a basin.

basin.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Celtic *baskis
Gaulish *baskisder.
Latin bacca
Vulgar Latin *baccinum
Old French bacinbor.
Middle English basyn
English basin
From Middle English basyn, from Old French bacin, from Vulgar Latin *baccinum (“wide bowl”).

ex.en: This district forms a basin.
ex.ja: この地方は盆地になっている。

ex.en: The water in the basin has frozen solid.
ex.ja: 洗面器の水がかちかちに凍った。

ex.en: A student was run over by a car on Basin Street.
ex.ja: １人の生徒がベイスン通りで車にひかれた。

en: Helpful or good to something or someone.
Receiving a benefit from something.
Something that provides a benefit.

beneficial.ety: From Late Latin beneficiālis (“beneficial”), from Latin beneficium (“benefit, favor, kindness”).

ex.en: Regular exercise is beneficial to good health.
ex.ja: 規則的な運動は健康によい。

ex.en: You should read books beneficial to you.
ex.ja: 君は自分のためになるような書物を読むべきだ。

ex.en: Your year-long stay in Germany was very beneficial, wasn't it?
ex.ja: あなたの１年間のドイツ滞在はとても有益でしたね。
